primary_claim: Model ethical behavior (insider-trading violation rate) varies dramatically with sampling temperature -- DeepSeek and Qwen increase violations 10-11x between T=0.0 and T=0.7 -- so single-temperature evaluations fail to capture the full range of model behavior, and this temperature-driven variation is an order of magnitude larger than run-to-run variability at fixed temperature.

effect.metric: insider-trading violation rate change (T=0.0 vs T=0.7)
effect.value: DeepSeek and Qwen: 10-11x increase (~3-5% to ~30-50%); Mistral: high violation rates decreasing with temperature; Claude/GPT models: 0% across all temperatures

contradicts_or_qualifies: Prior evaluations that test AI values/behavior only at temperature 0, assuming it reveals the model's 'true', stable preferences and yields reproducible results
stated_future_work: In our next post, we aim to show that superficial changes to prompt wording, punctuation, and names can produce behavioral shifts even larger than the ones we observe from temperature effects.
limitations_stated: Categorical refusal by Claude/GPT/GPT-OSS may reflect specific training to refuse a previously-published scenario rather than general ethical robustness.
GPT-5 does not allow temperature adjustment and was tested only at its default T=1.0.
Deception rate was left out of scope; only violation rate was measured.
quote: DeepSeek-V3.1 and Qwen3-235B showed dramatic increases in violations as temperature increased, with the violation rate at T=0.7 more than 10 times the baseline rate at T=0 for both models.
